column2: The planning layer, worked text-first from the WLC with Swete and Rahlfs alongside — the prose–poetry–prose frame and divine-name distribution, readings that matter (9:33; 13:15; 42:2, 10), the Greek Job, a five-movement arc with three contested seams, microscript, a three-part intertextual map (sources, self-quotation, later scripture), Christological trajectory, six preaching traps, the early↔late echo table and a seventeen-unit preaching plan.

The whole-book sweep through the seventeen preaching units, worked from the WLC with Swete and SBLGNT alongside — chapter 3 answered in God's speeches, speech to God as the verdict's hinge, the lawsuit vocabulary, the mediator trajectory ending in Job's intercession, and ten book-overview tensions for the Finalise pass.

Superseded by the Job 1:1–3:1 unit report; kept as the verse-level record. Solo dig on the prologue (Unit 1), worked from the WLC with Swete and SBLGNT alongside: the "bless" hinge, Job falling to worship where disaster fell, Abraham's test behind Job's, the Accuser speaking Deuteronomy's blessing formula, and a corrected count for the Satan.

Superseded by the Job 1:1–3:1 unit report; kept as the verse-level record. Solo dig on the second test (Unit 2), worked from the WLC with Swete and SBLGNT alongside: God's admission "without cause", the wife repeating God's words, the covenant curse (Deut 28:35) and the plague gesture (Exod 9), evil received from God, and the friends' seven silent days.

Unit report for Sermon 1 (Job 1:1–3:1), consolidating the two prologue digs: five scenes alternating earth and heaven, one question tested twice and answered with its own word, six "blesses" and one real curse — on his day — and 3:1 as the hinge where the Hebrew closes and the Greek opens.

Claim audit of the book's macro-structure for a sermon series: Patrick's nine units and James Bejon's (Tyndale House, 2020) fivefold scenes and vayomer acts, tested against the WLC formulas, Leningrad paragraphing, the accent register and the Old Greek, with a recommended nine-sermon plan.

Sermon backbone for Sermon 1 (Job 1:1–3:1, ESV pulpit): is God worth fearing for nothing? Four movements — the question heaven asks, "blessed be the name", good and evil from God, silence and a cry — landing on the Servant hated without cause.

Sermon backbone for the introductory sermon on the whole book (ESV pulpit): the question "for no reason?" (1:9) and God's verdict (42:7–8) — the servant who spoke to God spoke rightly; the friends who spoke for God spoke folly. Includes a mechanical check that no friend or Elihu ever addresses God.

Solo dig and unit report for Sermon 2 (Job 3, ESV pulpit), worked from BHS with the WLC, Swete and SBLGNT: the curse on the day, not God, in the words of Genesis 1 reversed and the plague of darkness; a lament addressed to no one that becomes prayer at 10:18; the rest the dead have and Job lacks; and God's speeches answering the chapter word for word.

Sermon backbone for Sermon 2 (Job 3:1–26, ESV pulpit): can you say the worst thing to God and not lose him? Three movements following the stanzas — "let the day perish", "why did I not die at birth?", "why is light given?" — and a short landing: the cry turned to God (10:18), God's answer in the chapter's own words (38:8), and the Son's forsaken cry answered.

Solo dig on Job 9–10 (HIGH unit in Sermon 3; ESV pulpit), worked from BHS with the WLC, Swete and SBLGNT: the friends' doctrine turned into a lawsuit Job cannot win; God's words for Job (blameless, without cause) in his own mouth; two creation hymns; the turn from speech about God to speech to God, answered word for word at 40:2, 5, 8; and the umpire who is not there (9:33).
